original_input.problem_statement: Expense reimbursement is slow: claims pass through 2-3 manager approvals with no visibility into status, and Finance manually re-keys every claim into the accounting system, consuming hours of staff time each week.
target_users: Employees submitting expense claims, who currently have no visibility into where their claim is stuck
Approving managers in the 2-3 step approval chain
Finance Operations staff who manually re-key claims and chase approvers

competitor_matrix.name: Expensify
competitor_matrix.reasoning: Directly relevant alternative for the stated approval-chain and re-keying problem; widely known in this category.
competitor_matrix.positioning: Mainstream expense-management SaaS built for external, multi-company expense reimbursement, with receipt scanning and configurable multi-step approval workflows layered on top.
competitor_matrix.strengths: A mature, widely-adopted product with strong mobile receipt capture and broad integrations into major accounting systems, so re-keying elsewhere in a company's stack is largely eliminated.
competitor_matrix.weaknesses: Priced and featured for organizations managing external, multi-entity expense management at scale; heavier in feature surface and cost than a single organization's 2-3 step internal approval chain actually needs.

competitor_matrix.name: Manual spreadsheet + email tracking (status quo)
competitor_matrix.reasoning: The status quo is itself the most relevant 'competitor' — the input describes it directly.
competitor_matrix.positioning: The current internal process described in the input: expense claims routed by email through 2-3 sequential manager approvals, tracked ad hoc in spreadsheets rather than any purpose-built system.
competitor_matrix.strengths: Requires no new tooling cost or vendor evaluation, and every employee and approver is already familiar with how it works today.
competitor_matrix.weaknesses: Gives employees no visibility into where their claim is stuck, gives approving managers no dashboard of pending items, and forces Finance to manually re-key every claim into the accounting system — the exact pain points named in the problem statement.

tam.basis: The external market for the category of software this internal tool would substitute for.
tam.reasoning: Order-of-magnitude figure from general knowledge of the expense-management SaaS category.

sam.value: Not meaningfully estimable — this is a single-organization internal tool with no external customers
sam.basis: SAM ordinarily scopes a serviceable addressable market of customers a product could realistically sell to; an internal-only tool has no such market.
sam.reasoning: Honest gap rather than a fabricated figure.

som.value: Avoided vendor cost only, not independently estimated
som.basis: The realistic 'obtainable' value for an internal tool is cost avoidance versus buying CM-01 or an equivalent.
som.reasoning: Low confidence because no actual headcount figure or CM-01 quote was available.

industry_trends.statement: Growing adoption of digital, mobile-first approval workflows to replace manual/email-based internal approval chains across mid-size organizations.
industry_trends.reasoning: General category trend supporting why a purpose-built internal tool is a reasonable direction rather than continuing the status quo (CM-02).

customer_insights.insight: Employees submitting claims want real-time visibility into where their claim is stuck in the 2-3 step approval chain.
customer_insights.reasoning: Stated directly in the problem statement ('no visibility into where their claim is stuck').

pricing_benchmarks.subject: Expensify
pricing_benchmarks.price_point: Roughly $4-36 per active user per month depending on plan tier (illustrative, not independently re-verified)
pricing_benchmarks.reasoning: General knowledge of the per-seat SaaS pricing pattern typical for this competitor category.

strengths.reasoning: Derived from CM-01's weakness (over-featured for this use case) — a narrower internal tool avoids that overhead.
strengths.statement: A purpose-built internal tool can be scoped exactly to this org's approval chain, avoiding the cost and feature overhead of a general-purpose SaaS tool priced and built for external, multi-entity expense management.

weaknesses.reasoning: Inferred from the problem being currently solved manually (CM-02) — no internal precedent exists to build from.
weaknesses.statement: No existing internal tooling or team experience building approval-workflow software exists yet, so building this in-house starts from zero precedent.

opportunities.reasoning: Derived from CI-01 and CM-02's stated weakness (manual re-keying) being the input's most explicit pain point.
opportunities.statement: Eliminating Finance's manual re-keying into the accounting system is a clear, measurable efficiency win that the status quo does not offer.

threats.reasoning: Derived from CM-01 being a mature, already-adopted category of tool in many orgs.
threats.statement: If Expensify (CM-01) is already budget-approved elsewhere, a bespoke tool may seem duplicative even though it is better scoped to this specific approval chain.

data_sufficiency.rationale: Two alternatives were reviewed — the mainstream SaaS leader (Expensify) and the status-quo manual process — covering the realistic range of options for this internal approval-chain problem. Market sizing, industry trends, customer insights, and pricing benchmarks are each grounded, though thinner given this is an internal-only tool.
